# /document-history — Creates a structured history document from templates for significant work completed in the current session. Supports bug fixes, features, implementations, and migrations. Auto-detects type and title from git history when invoked without arguments. Fills in all template sections with concrete details from session context.

## When to Use

Invoke this command when the user requests or implies the
`document-history` operation.

## Purpose

Creates a structured history document from templates for significant work completed in the current session. Supports bug fixes, features, implementations, and migrations. Auto-detects type and title from git history when invoked without arguments. Fills in all template sections with concrete details from session context.

## Shared State

This command participates in the shared workflow state. Read and update:

- **AGENT_BACKLOG.md** — Prioritized work items; read before starting, update when adding/completing tasks
- **.windsurf/state/orchestrator.json** — Phase, team status, metrics; read for context
- **.windsurf/state/events.log** — Append a log line when completing significant actions

## Flags

| Flag        | Description                                                                                                                                                         | Default |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `--type`    | Document type. The four primary types are used directly; issue and lesson are typically created via /review --focus=retrospective but can also be created manually. | —       |
| `--title`   | Human-readable title for the document                                                                                                                               | —       |
| `--pr`      | PR number to reference in the document                                                                                                                              | —       |
| `--auto`    | Auto-detect type and title from recent git history                                                                                                                  | false   |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be created without writing files                                                                                                                    | false   |
